tools.name: search_liliphant_docs
tools.description: Search the Liliphant API documentation with a natural-language question. Returns the most relevant passages with their page URLs.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "how do I send a WhatsApp template message"

tools.name: get_liliphant_api_docs
tools.description: Browse the Liliphant API API docs, one level at a time. Call it without arguments to get the top level: the modules and pages with a short description and the endpoints they hold. Call it with `path` set to a module's or page's link (or path) to get what is inside it; each listing links the next level. Call it with `path` set to an endpoint's link ending in ".openapi.yml" to get that endpoint as an OpenAPI file: method, url, headers, query params, path variables, a request body example and sample responses. Fetch only the level you need.

path.description: A link from a listing, exactly as given (e.g. "https://docs.example.com/sms/llms.txt" or ".../sms/send-sms.openapi.yml"), or just the path ("sms", "sms/send-sms.openapi.yml"). Leave it out for the top level.

tools.name: call_any_read_api_of_liliphant
tools.description: Read from any Liliphant API API endpoint with a GET request for the user and return its response. Use it once you know the exact endpoint: look it up with get_liliphant_api_docs first to get its URL, headers, query params and body, unless the skill or a dedicated tool on this server already gives them exactly. Load the quickstart-liliphant skill first: it explains which tool to use when. For POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE use call_any_api_of_liliphant. Pass the full url with path variables filled in, the headers the docs list, and query params in `query` (not in the url). For the auth header the docs name (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...), pass it with an empty value "": the signed-in user's token is filled in automatically. Never put a real or made-up token there; if the docs name no auth header, leave it out and the token is sent as Authorization. If the API needs the user to sign in, they're asked the first time. Returns { status, ok, headers, data }: the HTTP status and the response body, including error details on failure.

url.description: Full endpoint URL with path variables replaced by real values, e.g. https://api.example.com/users/42. Put query params in `query`, not here.

headers.description: Request headers as name/value pairs, as the docs list them. Give the auth header (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...) an empty value "" so the signed-in user's token is filled in; never put a token here yourself. Pass {} when the endpoint needs no headers. Example: {"proxy_auth_token": "", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

query.description: Query params as name/value pairs; an array sends the param once per item. Example: {"type": "flow", "bringflows": true}

tools.name: call_any_api_of_liliphant

Use it once you know the exact endpoint: look it up with get_liliphant_api_docs first to get its URL, headers, query params and body, unless the skill or a dedicated tool on this server already gives them exactly. Load the quickstart-liliphant skill first: it explains which tool to use when. For GET requests use call_any_read_api_of_liliphant. For the auth header the docs name (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...), pass it with an empty value "": the signed-in user's token is filled in automatically. Never put a real or made-up token there; if the docs name no auth header, leave it out and the token is sent as Authorization. If the API needs the user to sign in, they're asked the first time. Returns { status, ok, headers, data }: the HTTP status and the response body, including error details on failure.

url.description: Full endpoint URL with path variables replaced by real values, e.g. https://api.example.com/users/42. Put query params in `query`, not here.

headers.description: Request headers as name/value pairs, as the docs list them. Give the auth header (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...) an empty value "" so the signed-in user's token is filled in; never put a token here yourself. Pass {} when the endpoint needs no headers. Example: {"proxy_auth_token": "", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

query.description: Query params as name/value pairs; an array sends the param once per item. Example: {"type": "flow", "bringflows": true}

method.description: HTTP method from the endpoint's docs

tools.name: get_me
tools.description:
Returns who is signed in and every company they can open, with their role in each. This is the first call a client makes after sign-in: almost every other call needs a company id from companies[].id.

Any signed-in person may call it. It also does housekeeping on the way: it makes sure the person's personal company exists and turns any email invitations waiting for them into memberships, so a company someone was just added to shows up here.

The x-company-id header is optional here. currentCompanyId tells you which company the server will use for requests that send this header; with no header, or one naming a company the person is not in, it falls back to their personal company instead of failing.

Other fields: companyLimit is how many companies a person may create (null means no limit) and companiesCreated is how many they have created so far, for a "New company" button. onboardedAt on each company is null until its setup is finished. paused on each company lists what a Liliphant admin has stopped there because it costs money (recording, processing, ask, automations); empty means nothing is, and ask means AI answers are refused, so a screen can say so instead of offering them. operator is true for the people who may open the admin panel. logoUrl and brandColor appear on a company whose profile has a website that Things of Brand knows; both are left out otherwise. hasMeetings is true once the current company has at least one meeting (one still being processed counts); until then the app shows only the first-meeting screen and Settings.

Errors: 401 NOT_SIGNED_IN when no token is sent; 401 SESSION_EXPIRED when the token is no longer valid.

tools.name: list_meetings
tools.description:
Lists the analysed meetings the caller may see, as cards, newest first, with the filter choices the Meetings screen offers. Use it to show or search the meeting list, and to find a meetingId for Get Meeting, Get Meeting Transcript, Get Share Link or the notes routes (meetings[].id).

Any member of the company may call it, but what comes back depends on their role. An owner or admin sees every meeting in the company. A member sees only the meetings they booked or were invited to, plus every meeting of each team they are in (only their own when they are in no team). It never returns meetings from a company other than the one named in x-company-id.

Paging: send limit (1 to 100) to get pages. When there are more results, nextCursor holds a token; pass it back as cursor to get the next page. nextCursor is null on the last page. Without limit, every matching meeting comes back in one response. Never build a cursor yourself.

The first page (no cursor) also carries the extras: filters (the types, tags, people and teams that actually occur, each with a count), totals (all meetings the caller may see, and how many of them still need attention, ignoring the filters) and processing (up to 50 meetings the caller may see that are still being analysed, newest first). On later pages filters and totals are null and processing is empty, so keep the first page's copy. meetingCount is the number of matches across all pages. In filters.people, team is true for someone who was ever on the company's side of a call.

Filters combine: q searches title, headline, summary, type, tag, a participant's name or email, a team's name, or an exact meeting id; type, tag and person take values from filters; teamId limits to meetings booked by or with that team's members (an id from filters.teams[].value); within keeps meetings from the last N days; from and to pick a custom date range instead; status is open (still needs something) or handled.

Team filter: an owner or admin may pass any of the company's teams. A member may pass only a team they are in, and filters.teams lists only their teams.

A company with no meetings gets an empty list, not an error.

Errors: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED when a query value is out of range, a date cannot be read, or the cursor is not one this server issued; 401 when not signed in or the sign-in expired; 404 TEAM_NOT_FOUND when teamId is not one of this company's teams, or (for a member) not a team they are in.

q.description: Optional. Free-text search, up to 200 characters. Matches title, headline, summary, type, tag, a participant's name or email, a team's name, or an exact meeting id

to.description: Optional. End of a custom date range, a date or date-time (ISO 8601), exclusive

tag.description: Optional. A tag, a value from filters.tags[].value

from.description: Optional. Start of a custom date range, a date or date-time (ISO 8601), inclusive. Either end may be left open

type.description: Optional. Meeting type, a value from filters.types[].value, e.g. SALES, SUPPORT, PARTNERSHIP, MARKETING, INTERNAL

limit.description: Optional. Page size, 1 to 100. Omit to get every matching meeting at once

cursor.description: Optional. The nextCursor from the previous page. Omit for the first page

person.description: Optional. A participant's name, a value from filters.people[].value

status.description: Optional. open (still needs something) or handled

teamId.description: Optional. A team id from filters.teams[].value. Keeps meetings that team's members booked or were invited to. A member may only pass a team they are in

within.description: Optional. Whole number 1 to 3650: only meetings that started within this many days

recorded.description: Optional. mine returns only meetings the caller recorded on the Liliphant phone app (Add Phone Recording), newest first, still limited to what the caller may see. Used by the app's "Recorded on your phone" list

tools.name: ask_a_question
tools.description:
Answers a plain-language question from the company's processed meetings, with a headline, a short answer, an optional chart and the quotes it is based on. Use it whenever someone asks what was said, decided or promised in their meetings. Leave out meetingId to search every meeting the asker may see; set it to answer from one meeting only.

Who may call it: any member of the company. An owner or admin asks over every meeting in the company; a member asks only over the meetings they may see (ones they booked or were invited to, plus their teams' meetings). The company comes from the x-company-id header. meetingId comes from List Meetings (meetings[].id).

This is slow: a minute is normal and up to three minutes happens, so allow a long timeout.

A question it cannot answer is still a 200 with chart null and the reason in body: "No conversations in this company yet" when the company has no processed meetings or meetingId names a meeting that does not exist or that the asker may not see; "No conversation covers that yet" when nothing matches; "Could not answer that" when the engine fails, with the reason in body and any failures in warnings and a "What went wrong" block in detail.

tags narrow a company-wide question to meetings carrying any of those tags or topic names. Each tag is normalised before matching: trimmed, upper-cased, spaces and underscores turned into dashes, other characters dropped, so "Renewal terms" matches the topic "Renewal terms". tags are ignored when meetingId is set.

id is the same for the same question (case and spacing ignored) and the same meetingId, so it can be used to keep the answer on the board with Keep Question on Board. Quotes are only traced to transcript lines in this company's meetings; one that cannot be traced keeps its words with affiliation "from the conversation" and no meetingId.

Errors: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for a missing, too short or too long question, an empty or too long meetingId, a tag over 40 characters or with no letter or digit, more than 10 tags, or any other field; 401 when the token is missing or expired; 403 SPENDING_STOPPED when a Liliphant admin stopped this company's AI answers.

tools.name: quickstart-liliphant
tools.description: Liliphant API quickstart: read the user's meetings and ask questions answered from what people actually said. Load before any Liliphant task. Call this to load the full instructions for this skill before doing the task.
